title: Commentary
intro: One remark per word, in the learner's language, from one call per lesson. The pick (★) is shown first; tap “other candidates” for the rest. Rate the pick, and any candidate you would rather have heard. 50 words, 51 candidates (1.0 a word). Picked two for 0, abstained on 0. 30 candidates flagged as factual. By kind: contrast 26, culture 7, register 6, mnemonic 6, false_friend 5, pronunciation 1

items.sub: Context is everything here: applied to a project it means getting your hands dirty, but directed at a person, it means to grope them.
More formal than 'pero'. Unlike 'pero', 'sin embargo' is usually isolated by commas or placed after a semicolon or period.
Watch out: Spanish uses the verb 'to have' with reason where English uses 'to be right'. Never say *estar correcto* for a person.

cards.title: girar en torno a — revolve around

items.sub: Sounds slightly more formal than 'centrarse en' and is predominantly used for abstract ideas rather than physical rotation.

cards.title: meterse en una conversación — to jump into a conversation

items.sub: Can be used neutrally when politely chiming in, or critically when someone is rudely eavesdropping or intruding without an invitation.
Stronger than 'necesario'. While 'necesario' means something is needed, 'imprescindible' literally means you cannot do without it.
When followed by 'en', it changes meaning to either be rich in something or to elaborate on and agree with a specific point.
Describes being thoroughly saturated, unlike the broader 'mojado' which can mean anything from damp to dripping.
Imagine a soggy piece of paper pulp or porridge, which comes from the Latin root behind 'empapar'.
Unlike 'raro' or 'extraño', which often imply something is bizarre, 'inusual' is more objective, simply meaning infrequent or out of the ordinary.

cards.title: acabar de — to have just done

items.sub: Used with an infinitive in the present tense to mean 'to have just done', but in the preterite, it shifts to 'to finish doing'.
It conjugates like 'decir' in most tenses, but watch out: the future and conditional are regular, like 'predeciría', not *prediré*.
Often shortened to just 'el cepillo' when the context of brushing teeth is already clear, or 'cepillo dental' on packaging.
Used specifically for missing opportunities or time, whereas actively squandering money or physical resources prefers 'malgastar' or 'despilfarrar'.
This is the formal or technical word. For everyday speech, people usually say 'al azar'.
Imagine multi-tasking while driving and getting a huge fine.
Picture a guy named Gary pulling off a clever trick to deceive everyone.
Unlike 'sacudir', which is a gentle dusting, 'zarandear' implies a rough, violent shake.
This is getting a tan; don't confuse it with 'quemarse', which means getting painfully sunburned.
Don't be fooled—this means a speech, not a polite conversation or discussion.
In Argentina, calling someone 'un perejil' means they are a scapegoat or a nobody.
That's the mustache on the lip, not the 'barba' on the chin.
Notice that 'hacer el ridículo' means to make a fool of yourself.
Use this for something touching and tear-jerking, unlike 'emocionante', which is thrilling or exciting.
While 'pelota' works for most balls, many regions prefer 'balón' for big sports balls.
In business, asking for 'un presupuesto' usually means asking for a price quote, not a budget.
В отличие от mystery или enigma, которые обозначают реальные жизненные загадки, riddle — это именно словесная головоломка.
Не путайте с congenital — «врождённый»! Здесь корень другой, он означает приятное сходство и дружелюбие.
В отличие от высокотонного scream, bellow — это всегда раскатистый, утробный рев, как у быка или разъяренного человека.
Blush — это краска на лице именно от стыда и смущения, а flush бывает от жары, бега или гнева.
Так называют решение, где нет чётких правил, и всё зависит исключительно от вашей личной интуиции и оценки.
Представьте пустой ствол дерева — «гол» внутри, как пустые ворота. Hollow — полый, пустой.
Это разговорный сленг: сказать «I'm a goner» значит признать, что вам конец, спасения больше нет.
В повседневной речи англоязычные люди скорее скажут laziness, а sloth звучит книжно или означает животное.
Это слово постоянно звучит в спортивных новостях. Обычно говорят «to suffer a concussion» — получить сотрясение.
Это слово чуть более литературное, чем crowd, и подчёркивает, что толпа очень плотная и движется.
В отличие от долгой любви, infatuation — это слепая, безумная страсть, которая вспыхивает мгновенно и быстро гаснет.
В отличие от простого быстрого движения, frantically всегда несёт оттенок паники, хаоса и отчаяния.
Запомните частую фразу «vicious circle» — порочный круг, из которого невозможно выбраться.
В отличие от обычного 'quickly', это слово означает паническую спешку, суету и хаос.
Это официальное слово. В повседневной речи лучше использовать просто 'give up'.
Представьте «гиппопотама», который притворяется вегетарианцем, а сам ест мясо — настоящий лицемер.
В отличие от 'bite', когда кусают один раз и уверенно, 'nibble' — это щипать, есть маленькими кусочками.
Полная противоположность этого слова — 'vice', то есть порок.
Слово начинается с отрицания 'in-' и похоже на 'mount' — гору, которую невозможно перешагнуть.
Это не просто внезапный 'fear' или 'terror', а долгое, давящее чувство тревоги перед будущим.
Не путайте с 'forgive': простить можно, а вот 'condone' значит молча поощрять или закрывать глаза на плохой поступок.
Не путайте с русской «фракцией» в смысле химического состава — здесь это политическая группировка.
«Deny» — это просто отрицать вину, а «refute» — именно опровергать чужие слова железными доказательствами.
Отличие от «flush»: blush всегда от стыда и смущения, а flush может быть от жары или гнева.
В отличие от 'pride', которое может означать гордыню, 'dignity' — это всегда внутреннее благородство и самоуважение.

groups.title: The prompt and the four calls

details.body:
You write the commentary for an audio vocabulary programme. Music plays, a native presenter says
each Spanish word and its translation, and after some words the **guide** adds one short
remark in English, the learner's own language. That remark is the only talk in the
programme, so it has to earn its place: it should make the word more memorable, or clearer, in a
few seconds. Chatter, filler and praise are worthless here.

These are the kinds of remark:

- `register`: how blunt, polite, slangy or formal the word is, and what to say instead in the other
  register. "The blunt way to say it; in polite company, say…"
- `contrast`: how it differs from a word the learner could confuse it with.
- `false_friend`: it looks or sounds like a English word and means something else.
- `pronunciation`: one concrete thing to listen for, such as a sound, the stress, or a silent letter.
- `mnemonic`: a keyword or image that links the sound to the meaning. It must be vivid and
  concrete, and it may be absurd.
- `joke`: a pun, an absurd image or a wry observation that makes you smile at the word.
- `culture`: where, when or by whom it is really said.

For each word below:
1. Write **candidates** for every kind that genuinely fits this word, and only those. One or two
   kinds fit most words, and none fits only a few. Each candidate is **at most 25 words**, spoken
   by the guide in English, and may quote the Spanish word. It never repeats the
   translation the listener has just heard.
2. Mark `factual: true` on any candidate that states a fact that could be wrong: an etymology, a
   regional claim, a usage statistic. Base facts on the notes given with the word, and do not
   invent an etymology. A candidate that is only a mnemonic, a joke or an image is never factual.
3. **Pick** the one candidate that would do the most for this word, by its index. Pick two only
   when both are strong and of different kinds.
4. Abstain, with an empty `pick` and a short `abstain` reason in English, only when every candidate
   would be filler. Try hard first: a good mnemonic or joke can be made for almost any word.

Answer with a JSON object and nothing else:

{"words": [{"headword": "...", "candidates": [{"kind": "...", "text": "...", "factual": false}], "pick": [0], "abstain": ""}]}

[
 {
  "headword": "meter mano",
  "primaryGloss": "to step in",
  "shortGloss": "to step in; to intervene; to grope",
  "pos": "idiom",
  "register": "colloquial",
  "topics": [
   "Actions"
  ],
  "definition": "Intervenir en un asunto, proyecto o mecanismo para modificarlo, arreglarlo o resolverlo.",
  "notes": [
   "Context is critical for this idiom: when applied to a task, project, or problem (\"meter mano a un asunto\"), it means to step in, take action, or get one's hands dirty.",
   "When directed toward a person (\"meterle mano a alguien\"), it almost always carries a sexual connotation meaning to grope or feel someone up."
  ]
 },
 {
  "headword": "sin embargo",
  "primaryGloss": "however",
  "shortGloss": "however; nevertheless",
  "pos": "phrase",
  "register": "neutral",
  "topics": [
   "Misc"
  ],
  "definition": "Locución que se utiliza para introducir una objeción, contraste o límite a lo que se acaba de decir.",
  "notes": [
   "More formal than 'pero'. Unlike 'pero', 'sin embargo' is usually isolated by commas or placed after a semicolon or period."
  ]
 },
 {
  "headword": "tener razón",
  "primaryGloss": "right",
  "shortGloss": "to be right; to be correct",
  "pos": "idiom",
  "register": "neutral",
  "topics": [
   "Misc"
  ],
  "definition": "Estar en lo cierto o sostener una opinión o juicio acertado.",
  "notes": [
   "Spanish uses the verb tener (to have) with razón (reason) where English uses 'to be right'. Do not use *estar correcto* or *ser correcto* for a person—correct or incorrect apply to answers, statements, or objects, while people 'have reason' (tienen razón)."
  ]
 },
 {
  "headword": "girar en torno a",
  "primaryGloss": "revolve around",
  "shortGloss": "to revolve around; to center on",
  "pos": "phrase",
  "register": "neutral",
  "topics": [
   "Misc"
  ],
  "definition": "Tener como tema principal, eje o motivo central a alguien o algo.",
  "notes": [
   "Used mainly in a figurative sense to indicate the central subject, theme, or focus of a conversation, story, controversy, or system.",
   "Similar to *centrarse en* (to focus on) or *girar alrededor de* (to revolve around), though *en torno a* sounds slightly more formal and is predominantly used for abstract ideas rather than physical rotation."
  ]
 },
 {
  "headword": "meterse en una conversación",
  "primaryGloss": "to jump into a conversation",
  "shortGloss": "to jump into a conversation; to butt in",
  "pos": "phrase",
  "register": "neutral",
  "topics": [
   "Social"
  ],
  "definition": "Intervenir o participar en una charla entre otras personas, a veces sin haber sido invitado.",
  "notes": [
   "Used both neutrally or politely (when excusing oneself to chime in) and critically (when someone is intruding or eavesdropping without invitation)."
  ]
 },
 {
  "headword": "imprescindible",
  "primaryGloss": "essential",
  "shortGloss": "essential; indispensable",
  "pos": "adj",
  "register": "neutral",
  "topics": [
   "Misc"
  ],
  "definition": "Dicho de una persona o cosa: de la que no se puede prescindir; totalmente necesario.",
  "notes": [
   "Stronger than \"necesario\". While \"necesario\" means something is needed, \"imprescindible\" literally means you cannot do without it (from the verb \"prescindir\")."
  ]
 },
 {
  "headword": "abundar",
  "primaryGloss": "to abound",
  "shortGloss": "to abound; to be plentiful",
  "pos": "verb",
  "register": "neutral",
  "topics": [
   "Misc"
  ],
  "definition": "Haber o existir en gran cantidad.",
  "notes": [
   "When followed by 'en', it can mean either 'to be rich in' (e.g. 'un río que abunda en peces') or 'to elaborate on / agree with an idea' (e.g. 'abundar en el mismo punto')."
  ]
 },
 {
  "headword": "empapado",
  "primaryGloss": "soaked",
  "shortGloss": "soaked; drenched",
  "pos": "adj",
  "register": "neutral",
  "definition": "Que está completamente lleno de agua o de otro líquido.",
  "notes": [
   "Comparison: 'empapado' describes being thoroughly saturated. 'Mojado' (wet) is broader and can mean anything from damp to dripping. 'Calado' emphasizes deep penetration, especially in the phrase 'calado hasta los huesos' (soaked to the bone).",
   "Etymology: Comes from the verb «empapar» (to soak), derived from the prefix «en-» (in/into) and the Latin word «papa» (pap/porridge), referencing the soft, thick consistency of soaked food."
  ]
 },
 {
  "headword": "inusual",
  "primaryGloss": "unusual",
  "shortGloss": "unusual; uncommon",
  "pos": "adj",
  "register": "neutral",
  "topics": [
   "Misc"
  ],
  "definition": "Que no es habitual, frecuente o común.",
  "notes": [
   "Unlike 'raro' or 'extraño', which often imply that something is weird or bizarre, 'inusual' is a more objective word meaning simply infrequent, atypical, or out of the ordinary."
  ]
 },
 {
  "headword": "acabar de",
  "primaryGloss": "to have just done",
  "shortGloss": "to have just done",
  "pos": "phrase",
  "register": "neutral",
  "topics": [
   "Actions"
  ],
  "definition": "Haber realizado una acción muy poco tiempo antes del momento en que se habla.",
  "notes": [
   "Used with an infinitive (acabar de + infinitive) in the present or imperfect indicative to express that an action was completed moments earlier (\"to have just done\").",
   "In the preterite tense, it shifts meaning to \"to finish doing\" (e.g. \"Acabé de comer a las tres\")."
  ]
 },
 {
  "headword": "predecir",
  "primaryGloss": "predict",
  "shortGloss": "to predict; to foretell",
  "pos": "verb",
  "register": "neutral",
  "topics": [
   "Misc"
  ],
  "definition": "Decir o anunciar algo que va a suceder antes de que ocurra.",
  "notes": [
   "Conjugated like 'decir' in most tenses (predigo, predices, predijo, predicho), but regular in the future and conditional (predeciré, predeciría, not prediré) and in the singular affirmative imperative (predice, not predí)."
  ]
 },
 {
  "headword": "el cepillo de dientes",
  "primaryGloss": "toothbrush",
  "shortGloss": "toothbrush",
  "pos": "noun",
  "register": "neutral",
  "topics": [
   "Health"
  ],
  "definition": "Utensilio con cerdas pequeñas que se usa con pasta dental para la higiene de la boca y los dientes.",
  "notes": [
   "Often shortened to just 'el cepillo' when the context of brushing teeth is already clear. You may also see 'cepillo dental', especially on product packaging or in clinical contexts."
  ]
 },
 {
  "headword": "desaprovechar",
  "primaryGloss": "waste",
  "shortGloss": "to waste; to miss (an opportunity)",
  "pos": "verb",
  "register": "neutral",
  "topics": [
   "Actions"
  ],
  "definition": "No aprovechar algo o no sacar el debido rendimiento o beneficio de una ocasión o recurso.",
  "notes": [
   "Direct antonym of 'aprovechar' (to take advantage of, make the most of).",
   "Used specifically for failing to make good use of opportunities, time, talent, or advantages. To express actively squandering money or resources, 'malgastar' or 'despilfarrar' is often preferred."
  ]
 }
]
